title: pyproject.toml has no [build-system] table -- project never actually installs as a package
description: uv sync/uv run report: 'Skipping installation of entry points (project.scripts) for package devops-deployment-metrics because this project is not packaged; to install entry points, set tool.uv.package = true or define a build-system'. pyproject.toml has never had a [build-system] table -- the [tool.uv.build-backend] section (recently fixed from a [tools.uv.build-backend] typo) has no effect without one. This was masked previously because noxfile.py's sessions always ran session.install(".") explicitly (pip's legacy setuptools fallback), which does build/install the project even with no [build-system] declared. Without nox forcing that install, 'uv run python -m xdoctest --modname=devops_deployment_metrics' fails with ModuleNotFoundError, and the devops-deployment-metrics CLI entry point is never installed either. mypy and sphinx autodoc are likely affected the same way.
acceptance_criteria: pyproject.toml has a [build-system] table selecting uv_build; 'uv sync' installs devops-deployment-metrics as an actual package (uv pip list shows it, and 'uv run python -c "import devops_deployment_metrics"' succeeds); 'make xdoctest' passes; the devops-deployment-metrics console script is installed and runnable via 'uv run devops-deployment-metrics --help'.
close_reason: Added [build-system] table selecting uv_build; project now installs as a real package. Also dropped dead safety dep, added pip-audit as a real dev dep, removed .cookiecutter.json, fixed audit target cleanup-on-failure. Verified: uv sync installs the package, console script works, make test/xdoctest/docs/lint all pass.

title: Remove vulnerable transitive nltk dep by dropping superseded 'safety' package (gh-security 114, 96, 111)
description: Dependabot security alerts #114, #96, #111 (all CRITICAL) flag nltk pickle-deserialization/RCE and JVM-argument-injection vulnerabilities: 'https://github.com/flexion/devops-deployment-metrics/security/dependabot/114', '.../96', '.../111'. nltk is not a direct dependency of this project -- it's pulled in transitively by 'safety' (pyproject.toml dev group, line ~52), which ADR-0017 already decided to replace with pip-audit (which is already configured and running in CI as the 'pip-audit' check). 'safety' was apparently never actually removed after that decision. Alerts #114/#96 need nltk>=3.10.3; #111 needs nltk>=3.10.0 -- but rather than force-bumping a transitive dep of a tool we no longer use, remove 'safety>=2.3.5' from the dev dependency group entirely, which drops nltk from the dependency tree and resolves all three alerts at the root cause, per the existing ADR.

acceptance_criteria: pyproject.toml no longer lists 'safety'; uv.lock no longer contains 'nltk' or 'safety'; nox -s pre-commit and the pip-audit session both still pass; Dependabot alerts #114, #96, #111 auto-close once the fix lands on main (dependency no longer present).

title: Add zizmor security scanning of GitHub Actions workflows
description: flexion/flexion-opp-capture's .github/workflows/ci.yaml has a 'zizmor' job that statically audits GitHub Actions workflows for security anti-patterns (script injection via untrusted inputs, overly broad permissions, unpinned actions, secret exfiltration risks, etc.) -- complementary to actionlint (which this repo already runs via pre-commit) but security-focused rather than syntax/style-focused. Their pattern: a dedicated job with harden-runner (egress-policy: block, allowed-endpoints incl. api.github.com/pypi.org/files.pythonhosted.org/github.com/release-assets.githubusercontent.com), astral-sh/setup-uv, then 'uvx zizmor==<pinned version> --min-severity high .github/workflows/*.yaml'. Add an equivalent job to this repo (matching this repo's harden-runner allowed-endpoints style and pinned-SHA action versions), covering both .yml and .yaml workflow files here (this repo mixes extensions).
acceptance_criteria: A zizmor job runs in CI on PRs/pushes to main, scanning .github/workflows/*.yml and *.yaml with --min-severity high (or whatever threshold is chosen), pinned to a specific zizmor version; harden-runner egress allowlist covers whatever hosts zizmor and uvx need; any high-severity findings on the current workflows are triaged and either fixed or explicitly accepted before merging this task.

title: Fix unescaped dot in .env-blocking regex (gh-772)
description: scripts/block-files.sh uses grep -q "^.env$" to block committing a literal '.env' file, but the unescaped '.' matches any single character, so it also matches files like 'Xenv' or '-env' while still working for '.env' itself (a false-negative risk is low here since it's over-matching, not under-matching, but it's still a real regex bug per gh-772). Escape the dot: "^\.env$".
design: Single-character fix: ^.env$ -> ^\.env$ in the grep pattern.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/block-files.sh uses an escaped dot (^\.env$); grep only matches a literal '.env' path; a file named e.g. 'Xenv' is no longer matched; existing .env-blocking behavior still works; nox -s pre-commit passes.

title: Replace markdownlint-cli with rumdl in pre-commit config
description: The .pre-commit-config.yaml markdownlint hook currently runs via a Docker image (ghcr.io/igorshubovych/markdownlint-cli:v0.31.1, language: docker_image), which is slow (pulls a container per run) and the Docker dependency is itself an extra CI/local surface. rumdl (https://github.com/rvben/rumdl) is a Rust-reimplementation of markdownlint with a native pre-commit hook (no Docker required) and claims drop-in rule compatibility. Evaluate whether rumdl's rule set covers what .markdownlint.json/.markdownlintignore currently configure, swap the pre-commit hook, translate the config as needed, and confirm 'make lint' (or 'pre-commit run --all-files') still catches the same class of issues on this repo's existing docs.
acceptance_criteria: .pre-commit-config.yaml's markdownlint hook is replaced with rumdl's pre-commit hook (no docker_image language); .markdownlint.json config (or equivalent) is translated to rumdl's config format if the rule names/options differ; 'make lint' passes and still flags real markdown issues (spot-check by temporarily introducing a violation); README/CONTRIBUTING mentions of markdownlint updated if any exist.
